title: A pagination whose final partial page is short by one, and a walk that loses its size
why: The change carries two coupled defects, and a reviewer has to name both. The clamp reads as a guard and is off by one, so the last page loses its item, and an entirely short final page becomes empty. At the same time all_pages stops forwarding size to last_page_number, so the wrong number of pages is walked whenever the caller passes a size of their own. Fixing one alone leaves the other: correct the bound and the walk still enumerates the pages of the default size; correct the forwarding and the last page is empty. The case scores a recall only when both are named, which is what the earlier version could not do. An even earlier version was itself defective: it forced the return type to a list and evaluated the truthiness of the sequence, and all three models found those regressions for real.

trusted.note: Both revisions read line by line. before/ walks every page correctly at any size; after/ plants exactly the two coupled defects, and nothing else differs. The pair was taken from a real review: recette #12 found that all_pages forwards size to page() but not to last_page_number(), and that the two fixes must ship together.

planted.problem: The clamp subtracts one too many, so the final page drops its last item, and a final page of one item is empty
all_pages no longer forwards size to last_page_number, so a caller with its own size gets the page count of the default
